memory_update.text: HSTM should be prioritized in later layers as the clearest underfollowed public supplier to healthcare-licensure capacity because clinical rotations, credentialing, learning, onboarding, and student-health-system matching are directly tied to program throughput.

LOPE remains the best reference anchor for the ABSN/OTA/hybrid-program capacity node, supported by provided evidence on partner programs, simulation technology, VR, prerequisites, and licensure-linked fields.

ATGE is a direct healthcare-education capacity operator; later diligence should focus on clinical placement constraints, pass rates, employer partnerships, and federal student-aid/regulatory sensitivity.

Most pure-play nursing simulation vendors, including Laerdal, Gaumard, Elevate Healthcare/CAE Healthcare, Ascend Learning/ATI, UWorld, Relias, and many clinical-placement tools, appear private or embedded in large diversified parents; public-market mapping is therefore sparse and may require supplier/customer triangulation.
CAE should not be treated as current healthcare-simulation exposure after its February 2024 sale of CAE Healthcare to Madison Industries; keep it only as historical context or false-positive memory.

For this node, the chokepoint evidence to verify is not generic online enrollment; it is clinical rotation availability, simulation substitution allowances, program approvals, faculty/preceptor capacity, licensure outcomes, and employer-linked healthcare workforce pipelines.

node: Healthcare licensure program capacity: nursing, OTA, counseling, social work, and related programs
summary: Expanded the healthcare-licensure capacity node into a two-lane stock universe. The cleanest underfollowed supplier candidate is HealthStream, because it sits at the clinical-rotation, student-to-health-system, credentialing, and healthcare workforce software layer rather than the obvious university-operator layer. Grand Canyon Education is retained as the reference anchor because provided evidence directly links it to ABSN/OTA partner programs, hybrid programs, simulation technology, virtual reality, prerequisite strategies, and licensure-linked workforce outcomes. Adtalem is a direct healthcare-education operator with Chamberlain, Walden, medical, veterinary, social work, and nursing exposure. Stride is a weaker second-order candidate through healthcare and medical certification training under MedCerts/Career Learning, but its link to licensed nursing/OTA capacity is less direct and needs verification.
